title: Which came first in the story of the decimal point?
description: Four events in the history of decimals are placed in order, from the eighth century to the sixteenth century. Each century is changed into its years so that the order can be read from the numbers. Keeko's doubt puts the sixteenth century first.
teaching_notes: One idea: change each century into its hundreds of years, and the bigger number is the later time. Watch for students who think the biggest century number is the earliest.

source: Order these events from earliest to latest: the 8th century
video_script.why: The child has read how decimals grew over time and now places the events in order using the size of the numbers.
video_script.substitution: Change each century into the hundreds of years it covers, then order the events from the smaller number to the bigger.
video_script.anchor: A timeline of the history of the decimal point, with four events to place in order.
video_script.wrong_move: Puts the sixteenth century first because sixteen is the biggest number, forgetting that a bigger century number is a later time.
video_script.payoff_line: A bigger century number is a later time

final_answer.spoken: eighth century, about nine hundred fifty of the common era, fifteenth century, sixteenth century

names.Leeza: an ancient Indian mathematician whose works from the eighth century used decimal fractions
names.Jia: an Arab mathematician whose book around the year nine fifty described decimal notation

maths_rules: a century is 100 years, and the 8th century is the 700s
950 CE is in the 900s, and 900s come after the 700s
the 15th century is the 1400s and the 16th century is the 1500s
700s < 950 < 1400s < 1500s, so the order is 8th century, about 950 CE, 15th century, 16th century
the slip: 16 is the biggest number, but the 16th century is the 1500s, which is later and not earlier
video_script.design: A timeline of years runs from left to right. Each century is changed into its hundreds of years and placed on the line, with the four events set in the order of the numbers. Keeko's slip is shown on the same line.
